title: Margin: why selling needs capital
summary: SPAN and exposure margin, return on margin, the strangle offset, and why overloading margin ends accounts.

questions.q: Why must option sellers post margin but buyers don't?
options: Sellers can lose far more than the premium they receive
questions.why: A buyer's loss is capped at the premium; a seller's is not, so the exchange blocks a safety deposit.

questions.q: Total margin for a short option in India is:
questions.why: Margin is the SPAN worst-case plus an exposure buffer.

questions.q: Premium ₹5,000, margin ₹1,25,000. Return on margin is:
Why does a short strangle usually need less margin than its two legs added together?
options: The exchange gives a discount to beginners
Both legs can't lose at the same time
questions.why: The stock can only move one way, so SPAN offsets the two legs' risk.

questions.q: The most common way new sellers lose an account is:
options: Overloading margin, so they can't hold a position through a move
questions.why: When margin rises and there are no free funds, positions get closed at the worst moment.
